Western and Central Atlantic (AL94): A non-tropical low pressure area located several hundred miles south-southeast of Bermuda is producing disorganized showers and thunderstorms. Recent satellite-derived wind data indicates a sharpening frontal structure is associated with this system. The low could still briefly acquire some subtropical characteristics through tonight, though this scenario appears to be trending less likely. 1. Eastern East Pacific: A broad area of low pressure is producing a large area of showers and thunderstorms. Recent satellite wind data indicates this system remains weak and disorganized. Some development is possible over the next day or two, but unfavorable environmental conditions should end formation chances early next week. Regardless of development, this system is expected to bring areas of heavy rain to portions of Central America through the weekend while it drifts northward. Formation chance through 48 hours...low...20 percent. Formation chance through 7 days...low...20 percent.
